Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ocean3d (development version)

Breaking changes

calc_volume_overlap() is removed (#150). It returned a nine-layer SpatRaster that the other 3D functions could only use as a flat 2D layer, not as the 3D space it described. Intersect with intersect_3d(), then measure with volume(), which has a new per_cell argument: volume(x, per_cell = TRUE) returns a one-layer SpatRaster named volume with the volume of each cell in km³, NA where x is absent. Each layer of the old stack maps to:

calc_volume_overlap(a, b) layer Now
depth_min_a, depth_max_a a itself (envelope), or voxel_to_envelope(a) (voxel)
depth_min_overlap, depth_max_overlap ov <- intersect_3d(a, b)
volume_a, volume_b volume(a, per_cell = TRUE), volume(b, per_cell = TRUE)
volume_overlap volume(ov, per_cell = TRUE)
0 where both are present but share no depth both <- !is.na(volume(a, per_cell = TRUE)) & !is.na(volume(b, per_cell = TRUE)), then terra::ifel(both & is.na(vol_ov), 0, vol_ov) with vol_ov <- volume(ov, per_cell = TRUE)
totals volume(a), volume(b), volume(ov)

Other changes to callers:

  • With an envelope and a voxel, calc_volume_overlap() reported the volume of the envelope after placing it on the voxel’s depth levels. volume() of the envelope uses its own depth limits. To compare it with the overlap on the same levels, use volume(envelope_to_voxel(a, depths(b), bounds = bounds, depth_bounds = depth_bounds(b)), bounds = bounds).
  • Cells with nothing in them are now NA everywhere. The old volume_overlap layer was the one place that used 0, for cells where both domains are present but share no depth; build that 0 from the inputs as in the table.
  • volume() of a domain with no cells now totals 0, not NA.
  • per_cell is the second argument of volume(), so a positional volume(v, "top") is now an error. Name it: volume(v, bounds = "top").
  • Pass the same bounds to intersect_3d() and volume(); otherwise the overlap and the input volumes are measured on different slabs and don’t add up.

bounds now defaults to "midpoint" instead of "top" in volume(), envelope_to_voxel(), intersect_3d(), intersects_3d() and mask() (#138). The slab of water each depth level stands for now runs halfway to the neighbouring levels. This matches World Ocean Atlas levels and is closer than "top" to Copernicus Marine layers. Under the old default each level was the top of its slab and the deepest level had no volume. Results change for voxels that don’t carry their own depth edges (see depth_bounds under New features):

  • volume() gives different volumes. For example, levels at 0, 100 and 300 m now stand for 0-50, 50-200 and 200-300 m rather than 0-100, 100-300 and none.
  • envelope_to_voxel() can place an envelope on different levels, and so can mask(), intersect_3d() and intersects_3d() when they combine an envelope with a voxel. An envelope from 60 to 70 m on levels at 0, 100 and 200 m now occupies the 100 m level rather than the 0 m one.

Pass bounds = "top" to keep the old results.

Point extraction (extract_to_point(), extract2d(), extract3d_*()) now checks the grid’s coordinates instead of assuming one layout (#74). Some calls that used to return a value now return NA or stop with an error:

  • By default (spatial_match = "within"), a point must lie inside a grid cell. Points outside the grid, which used to get the value of the nearest edge cell, now return NA. This includes observations near a single-station file that are not at the station itself. Use spatial_match = "nearest" with max_distance_km to accept nearby cells.
  • Observation depths must be metres, positive downward. Negative depths (heights) now stop with an error; convert them, and km or cm depths, before extraction.
  • Depth coordinates are converted to metres from their units, and the positive attribute sets their direction. Surface, bottom and nearest are chosen by physical depth, whether the coordinate is stored shallow to deep or deep to shallow. The depth coordinate must have length units, including for extract3d_surface() and extract3d_bottom(); files without them stop with an error. A file with a single depth level can be read with extract2d().
  • With several files, a temporal tie between sources keeps input order under "within" matching, and goes to the closer cell centre under "nearest" matching.

Point, track and buffer extraction now check cell bounds the same way, and stop with an error when they are bad (#113):

  • Each cell must have a positive width, contain its centre and not overlap another cell, and a bounds attribute must name a usable bounds variable. This applies to longitude and latitude bounds everywhere, and to depth and time bounds in buffer extraction. Horizontal buffers also reject longitude cells that overlap after wrapping around 360°. The error names the file.
  • Point and track extraction used to warn and infer longitude and latitude edges from the centres. They don’t read time bounds.
  • To read a file that now fails, fix its bounds, or remove the coordinate’s bounds attribute so edges are inferred from the centres (for example with NCO: ncatted -a bounds,lon,d,, file.nc).

Point and track extraction, and buffer extraction without a depth window (depth_radius_m = 0), used to accept a netCDF depth coordinate stored out of order (for example 50, 0, 100 m), and rejected only duplicate depths. They now stop with an error naming the coordinate and the file unless the depths run shallow to deep or deep to shallow (#147). Sort such files along the depth dimension before extraction. The error for longitude or latitude stored out of order, which already stopped extraction, now names the coordinate and the file too.

With return_match_info = TRUE, the bounds entry of the <output>_match_info column from extract_to_buffer() used to label longitude and latitude edges inferred from the centres "inferred_regular" or "inferred_irregular". Both now read "inferred_midpoints", the label depth and time already use, so the entry no longer says whether the spacing is regular (#147). Code that checks for the old labels should check for "inferred_midpoints".

vect_to_envelope() now stops with an error when the envelope would have no cells: no cell the polygons cover has depth_max deeper than depth_min. It used to warn and return an empty envelope, so code that loops over polygons and drops empty results has to handle the error instead. The message says how many cells have the limits swapped (or a seafloor above depth_min), equal, or missing (#114).

New features

  • New arguments spatial_match, max_distance_km, spatial_report and depth_report. Longitudes match across the 0-360 and -180-180 conventions and across the antimeridian.
  • Missing outputs are explained once, under the report for their cause (spatial, depth or time), with repeated reasons grouped by file. The time report now also explains outputs that are missing because no observation date was supplied for a file with a time dimension.
  • New experimental class SpatProxy, built with as_proxy(), describes one variable of a netCDF file without reading its values (#113): its axes, chunk sizes and coordinate reference system (CRS). Depth is in metres positive down and time is a CFtime object. as_proxy() stops with an error if the time axis isn’t strictly increasing or is a climatology. No other function accepts a SpatProxy yet, and it may change without notice.
  • New class SpatVector3D for 3D points, lines and polygons, built with as_vector3d() from a table, sf object or terra::SpatVector. Points and lines have a depth (positive metres down) and an optional time at each vertex (for sf lines, depth is minus Z and time is M). Polygons have a depth range, depth_min to depth_max, and an optional time interval per feature, such as a protected area from 0 to 200 m. geomtype() reports the type (#114).
  • New buffer_3d() turns each SpatVector3D point or line into a polygon with a depth range and an optional time interval, such as a circle of 10 km radius from 10 to 60 m deep around a detection at 35 m. volume() on points or lines now suggests it (#114).
  • New vector3d_to_envelope() puts SpatVector3D polygons onto a grid as a SpatEnvelope, as vect_to_envelope() does for 2D polygons. Where polygons overlap, a cell gets the shallowest top and deepest bottom of the polygons covering it, so polygons from 0 to 50 m and from 200 to 300 m give 0 to 300 m. Cells where top equals bottom are dropped, and so are polygon times, with a message (#114).
  • A SpatVoxel can carry the top and bottom of the slab of water each layer stands for, such as a netCDF file’s depth bounds: pass depth_bounds to as_voxel() or envelope_to_voxel(), and read them with the new depth_bounds(). volume(), calc_volume_overlap(), envelope_to_voxel(), intersect_3d(), intersects_3d() and mask() then use these edges instead of bounds. Results that stay a SpatVoxel keep the edges, including after c(); app() and writing to a file drop them. For such a voxel, voxel_to_envelope() gives each cell an envelope from the top of its shallowest selected slab to the bottom of its deepest, and the depth limits from calc_volume_overlap() follow the same rule (#138).

Bug fixes

  • netCDF time axes are decoded with the CFtime package. Time units that used to stop extraction are now read: a trailing UTC or Z (days since 2020-01-01 UTC), origins written 2020-1-1, 00:00:0.0 or without seconds, years before 1000 with the proleptic_gregorian calendar, and a single time step in months since units, as in World Ocean Atlas files (#88). A time axis of several months or years still stops with an error, because their length is ambiguous.
  • Reference dates before 1582-10-15 on the standard and gregorian calendars are accepted, such as hours since 1-1-1 00:00:0.0 in older NCEP reanalysis files; CFtime counts the Julian days before the calendar change. Time steps before 1582-10-15 on these calendars still stop with an error.
  • Time steps stored as fractional days (for example 10-minute data in days since 1970-01-01) decode exactly, so exact time matching no longer returns NA for observations on a file timestamp (#90).
  • A file passed as a connection opened with ncdf4::nc_open(readunlim = FALSE) now gives the same result as its path when the time dimension is unlimited (#92).
  • Files on calendars other than standard, gregorian and proleptic_gregorian (such as noleap or 360_day) still stop, now with an error that names the calendar.
  • Matching observation dates to long time axes is fast again: 500 dates against a 10-year daily file take about 0.35 s, down from about 11 s (#89).
  • A time step that appears more than once (for example after joining two files that overlap) no longer stops the whole extraction. It is an error only when an observation selects it, and the error names the file and the timestamp (#91).
  • An observation exactly halfway between two time steps takes the one on its own UTC day. Midnight date-times, as readxl::read_excel() returns for Excel dates, used to get the previous day on files stamped at noon (#71).
  • Files whose time bounds are back to back (one interval ends where the next starts, as in monthly means) no longer print CFtime’s “Offsets not monotonically increasing” warning in point and buffer extraction. Time bounds that don’t contain their time step still stop buffer extraction with an error (#113).
  • The axis and standard_name attributes of ordinary dimension coordinates are now read when longitude, latitude, depth and time are detected in point, buffer and track extraction. Files whose dimension names don’t say which axis is which (such as x labelled latitude) used to be read along the wrong axes without a warning, and an altitude dimension with axis = "Z" stopped with an “Unrecognised non-singleton dimension” error unless depth_dim was given (#93).
  • Curvilinear grids, such as native NEMO output with two-dimensional nav_lon / nav_lat coordinates, now stop with an error when those coordinates are identified only by their units (degrees_east, degrees_north). They used to be read with the grid indices as longitude and latitude. Regrid such data to a regular longitude/latitude grid first (#93).

Minor improvements

  • Functions that take a SpatEnvelope check it faster when it is held in memory. Envelopes read from a file, or with more than a million cells, are checked as before. On 9-cell test grids, as_envelope() is about 5 times faster, intersect_3d() about 2 times, volume() about 1.6 times and calc_volume_overlap() about 1.2 times (#154).

  • as_envelope()’s depth errors now come from the SpatEnvelope validity check, so they start with invalid class "SpatEnvelope" object: and use its wording: “depth_max must be at least depth_min in every cell”, and for negative depths “depths are positive metres increasing downward, but depth_min has negative values; if these are elevations, flip their sign first” (#154).

Dependencies

  • CFtime (>= 1.7.3) is now imported, for decoding CF time units.

ocean3d 0.1.1.9009

Housekeeping release addressing goodpractice checks (#58). Apart from the changes below, behaviour is unchanged.

Bug fixes

  • Point extraction functions (extract_to_point(), extract2d(), extract3d_*()) no longer drop netCDF sources when nc is a list that contains a data frame of file paths; previously the data frame replaced every source listed before it. A vector of paths inside a list is now accepted too.

Minor improvements

  • dplyr and gfwr move from Imports to Suggests; no package code uses them, so installing ocean3d no longer pulls them in.

ocean3d 0.1.1.9008

The copernicus_* family is withdrawn for now. It is not abandoned: the code is preserved on the feat/7-copernicus branch and in the history of this one, and it will return once it is properly covered by tests (#50).

Breaking changes

  • copernicus_setup(), copernicus_login(), copernicus_status(), copernicus_load(), copernicus_summarise(), copernicus_cache_dir() and copernicus_cache_clear() are removed. Code calling them should pin to 0.1.1.9007 or use the feat/7-copernicus branch.
  • ecmwfr and jsonlite are dropped from Imports, and reticulate and rstudioapi from Suggests; they were only ever used by the Copernicus backends. here moves out of Imports but stays in Suggests, where the vignette articles still use it.

ocean3d 0.1.1.9007

The package is renamed from sharkabc3d to ocean3d, to reflect that the 3D workflows apply to any marine taxon or spatial layer, not just sharks and rays.

Breaking changes

  • library(sharkabc3d) becomes library(ocean3d). No function names, arguments or class names changed — only the package name.
  • The WOA download cache moves with the package name, from tools::R_user_dir("sharkabc3d", "cache")/woa to tools::R_user_dir("ocean3d", "cache")/woa. Previously downloaded WOA files are not found at the new location; either re-download them or move the old woa directory across. woa_cache_dir() reports the new path.
  • Package Title and Description are broadened from “Shark and Ray Abiotic Covariates in 3 Dimensions” to “Three-Dimensional Marine Spatial Analysis”.
  • The repository and pkgdown site move to Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d; GitHub redirects the old URLs, but devtools::install_github() calls should be updated.
